author: praasz
title: iGPU func tests fail en masse - no supported GPU devices found on runner
signature: Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed: [GPU] Can't get <PROPERTY> property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU Tests (func) / GPU
failed_jobs.symptom: 32927/43254 GPU func tests failed immediately with 'no supported devices found' (clinfo reports 0 platforms)

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check failed because the iGPU Tests job failed

key_errors:
C++ exception with description "Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:272:
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:112:
Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed at src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593:
[GPU] Can't get DEVICE_TYPE property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query.
[GPU] Please check OpenVINO documentation for GPU drivers setup guide." thrown in the test body.
root_cause: The iGPU self-hosted runner reported 'Number of platforms 0' before any OpenVINO GPU test executed, meaning the OpenCL/Level-Zero driver stack inside the test container could not enumerate the Intel iGPU render device. Every GPU plugin test that queries a device property (DEVICE_TYPE, etc.) hits the '!m_device_map.empty()' assertion in src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593 and fails uniformly (32927 of 43254 tests). This is the exact same signature recorded ~1h15m earlier for run 39387885502 (commit 521ffc4d), confirming a persistent/recurring runner-level GPU driver or device-node availability problem rather than a regression from the triggering commit, which is a CMake-only refactor of the GPU plugin build (removing GLOB usage, PR #38655) unrelated to device enumeration.
reproduction_steps: N/A (requires the specific self-hosted iGPU runner/container image); cannot be reproduced without access to that runner's GPU driver stack. To check driver health on the runner: run 'clinfo' inside the test container and confirm 'Number of platforms' > 0.
recommended_actions: Escalate immediately to the self-hosted iGPU runner fleet owners: this is the second occurrence within ~1.5 hours, indicating the GPU driver/device-node issue has not been resolved since the prior investigation (run 39387885502).

Check the affected runner's Intel Compute Runtime / NEO, Level-Zero, and i915 kernel driver status - 'clinfo' reporting 0 platforms indicates the OpenCL ICD stack is broken or /dev/dri/renderD128 is inaccessible.
Restart or re-provision the affected iGPU runner(s); consider temporarily removing the runner from the pool until driver health is confirmed.
Add a pre-flight GPU-device-availability smoke check as the first step of the iGPU test job to fail fast instead of running and failing all ~43k tests individually.
prevention_strategies: Add a lightweight GPU-device-availability smoke check as the very first step of the iGPU test job (fail fast with a clear 'runner GPU unavailable' message) instead of letting all 43k tests run and fail individually. Monitor self-hosted iGPU runner fleet health (driver versions, device node permissions) with periodic health checks independent of CI runs, and alert on repeat occurrences automatically.
historical_context: Identical '!m_device_map.empty()' / 'no supported devices found' signature was recorded ~1h15m earlier for run 39387885502 (commit 521ffc4d, author hyunback) on 2026-10-20T09:11:02Z. This is now the 2nd occurrence of the same underlying iGPU runner/driver infrastructure issue in a short window, suggesting the earlier recommended remediation (driver/runner health check) was not yet applied or the runner has not recovered.
